# The Helix Center for Interdisciplinary Investigation
> A 501(c)(3) nonprofit that hosts free, public interdisciplinary roundtable discussions in New York City, bringing together Nobel laureates, MacArthur Fellows, and 500+ distinguished scholars since 2012.

## Organization
- Name: The Helix Center for Interdisciplinary Investigation
- Also known as: The Helix Center, Helix Center
- Type: 501(c)(3) Nonprofit Educational Organization
- Founded: 2012
- Location: 247 East 82nd Street, New York, NY 10028 (The Marianne & Nicholas Young Auditorium)
- Founder & Director: Dr. Edward Nersessian (psychoanalyst, clinical professor of psychiatry)
- Website: https://www.helixcenter.org/
- Mission: To foster interdisciplinary dialogue by convening leading thinkers from different fields for unscripted roundtable conversations, freely shared with the public

## Key Facts
- 507 unique distinguished speakers (2012-2026)
- 134+ roundtable discussions across 15 seasons
- 13 academic disciplines represented
- 50+ institutions including Columbia, NYU, Princeton, Yale, Harvard, MIT, Oxford, Cambridge, UCL
- 197 speakers (39%) have linked Wikipedia articles
- All events are free and open to the public
- All recordings freely available via website and YouTube

## Notable Participants
- Daniel Kahneman -- Nobel Prize in Economics (2002), Princeton University
- Eric Kandel -- Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (2000), Columbia University
- David J. Gross -- Nobel Prize in Physics (2004), UC Santa Barbara
- Christian de Duve -- Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine (1974), Rockefeller University
- Karl Friston -- Most-cited neuroscientist in history (h-index 291), University College London
- Sara Seager -- MacArthur Fellow, Kavli Prize in Astrophysics, MIT
- David Chalmers -- Formulated "the hard problem of consciousness," NYU
- Rosalind Picard -- Founder of Affective Computing, MIT Media Lab
- Sylvester James Gates -- National Medal of Science, University of Maryland
- Barry Mazur -- Chern Medal, Harvard University
- Vijay Iyer -- MacArthur Fellow, Harvard University
- Yiyun Li -- MacArthur Fellow, Princeton University
- Percival Everett -- Pulitzer Prize, University of Southern California
- Gyorgy Buzsaki -- The Brain Prize, NYU Neuroscience Institute

## The Theaetetus Table Format
The Helix Center's signature format is the "Theaetetus Table," named for the Platonic dialogue investigating the nature of knowledge. Five participants -- leaders in their respective fields -- gather for extempore (unscripted) interdisciplinary discussion. The five participants symbolize the five Platonic solids and cultivate: curiosity, playfulness, inspiration, reflection, and wonder.
